blocks.text: Kaikki, muutama, moni — these small quantifier words have drifted past unglossed since Lesson 6. They're what let a reviewer say 'everything', 'a few', 'many' without listing items one by one. This lesson rounds up the whole family.

blocks.title: Quantifiers as blame-spreading
blocks.text: When a reviewer reaches for kaikki (all/everything) instead of naming one specific fault, the complaint widens — it stops being about a single mistake and becomes about a pattern. Kaikki tekemänsä virheet lands very differently from yksi virhe, and reviewers choose their quantifier deliberately.

blocks.content: {Kaikki|grammar|quantifier|all/everyone/everything} covers 'all' in every sense — people, things, or a whole amount. It stays the same word whether it means 'everyone' or 'everything'; context decides which. Kaikki toimi hyvin — 'everything worked well'. Kaikki asiakkaat — 'all the customers'.

items.en: Everything worked well after the service.
All the customers got the same treatment.

blocks.text: Piece 2 — Moni, muutama, joku: many, a few, someone

blocks.content: {Moni|grammar|quantifier|many} means 'many'. {Muutama|grammar|quantifier|a few/a couple} means 'a few/a couple'. {Joku|grammar|quantifier|someone/some} means 'someone/some'. All three commonly pair with a partitive noun, following the same logic as Lesson 19's numbers — an unspecified amount reaches for the partitive.

items.en: Many a customer has told of the same problem.
A few elderly people were there at the same time.
Some part was changed without permission.

blocks.title: The one-by-one quantifier
blocks.text: {Jokainen|grammar|quantifier|each/every} singles things out one at a time, unlike kaikki's sweeping 'all'. Jokainen asiakas maksoi eri hinnan — 'each customer paid a different price' — emphasises the individual cases rather than the group as a whole.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Did they admit all the mistakes they made?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Eivät kaikkia. Muutama virhe myönnettiin, mutta moni jäi kiistanalaiseksi.
lines.en: Not all of them. A few mistakes were admitted, but many remained disputed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.fi: Onko joku muu asiakas kertonut samasta?
lines.en: Has some other customer told of the same thing?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Kyllä, jokainen arvostelu kertoo samaa tarinaa.
lines.en: Yes, every review tells the same story.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: Think of these five words on a spectrum from sweeping to specific: kaikki (all, sweeping) → moni (many) → muutama (a few) → joku (someone/some, vague) → jokainen (each, one at a time). Picking the right one on that spectrum is often the difference between a fair review and an unfair generalisation — and now you can read which one a reviewer chose.

blocks.content: Kaikki: KAIK-ki (short, double k held). Muutama: MUU-ta-ma (long held 'uu', three syllables). Jokainen: YO-kai-nen (the 'j' is a 'y' sound, three even syllables).
